ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Swami Vivekananda

code.originalText: Five-week diabetes review before a long journey: glucose log, metformin dose, kidney function and potassium on losartan, repeat urine albumin, retinal photographs, statin, and a travel and fasting plan

text.paragraph: Five-week diabetes review before a long journey. [S]

Swami Vivekananda returns five weeks after starting metformin and two weeks after starting losartan. His thirst has gone, he wakes to pass urine once a night or not at all, and his fasting readings are 128 to 150 mg/dL. He has had no dizziness on losartan; home blood pressure averages 128/80. He has seen the dietitian twice: he now takes a smaller portion of rice with more dal and vegetables, keeps the sweets offered after worship to a small piece, and has kept two fortnightly fasts with fruit, milk and water, with midday readings of 110 to 140 mg/dL. The screening tests from the preventive visit were negative for HIV, hepatitis C, hepatitis B surface antigen and tuberculosis infection, and he is not immune to hepatitis B. He has decided to take the statin. In a week he leaves for several months of travel and teaching in the mountains, and wants a plan he can follow far from the clinic. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-03-23; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 73.8 kg; blood pressure 128/80, pulse 74
Retinal photographs today: no retinopathy in either eye

Thirst, frequent urination day and night, tiredness and about 4 kg weight loss over two months, with a random glucose of 246 mg/dL; told by physicians a year ago that he had diabetes, never confirmed with modern tests or treated except by diet. Diabetes to be confirmed and classified (type 2, type 1 or slowly progressive autoimmune diabetes) with A1c, fasting glucose, GAD antibodies and C-peptide
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to his documented diabetes of the year before. Superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.

Type 2 diabetes: A1c 9.4 percent and fasting glucose 172 mg/dL, with symptoms; GAD65 antibodies negative and fasting C-peptide preserved (2.6 ng/mL); no ketones. BMI 24.6, in the range where ADA screens Asian Americans. Classified as type 2, not type 1 or slowly progressive autoimmune diabetes
S — Synthetic modern confirmation and classification linked to his documented diabetes.
Moderately increased albuminuria on a first sample (urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 46 mg/g), eGFR normal; to be confirmed on two of three samples over three to six months
S — Synthetic finding linked to his documented albuminuria; superseded when diabetic kidney disease was confirmed.
Raised blood pressure in clinic (138/86, average of two readings) without a diagnosis of hypertension; home readings to be taken
S — Synthetic finding; not a claim about his real blood pressure.
Hypertension, stage 1: clinic 138/86, 136/86 and 134/84; home average 136/86 over seven days; with moderately increased albuminuria and diabetes
S — Synthetic finding of the modern episode; not a claim about his real blood pressure, which was never recorded.

Long-standing difficulty falling asleep: by his own account he has never been able to fall asleep on getting into bed and lies awake for two hours or more most nights; worse lately with waking to pass urine; rises before dawn for meditation
S — Synthetic modern problem linked to his documented lifelong difficulty falling asleep.
Mixed hyperlipidemia: LDL cholesterol 132 mg/dL, triglycerides 228, HDL 36

list.item:
Type 2 diabetes, improving (E11.65). Improving on metformin 1000 mg and his changed diet, with fasting readings still above 130. He chose to increase metformin to the full dose. A second medicine (an SGLT2 inhibitor) was discussed; because his albuminuria is not yet confirmed, and because a new medicine that adds fluid loss is unwise at the start of months of travel with fasting, he chose to wait and decide on his return. [S]
Metformin extended-release 2000 mg with the evening meal.
A1c in three months: at a laboratory where he is staying, or a home kit, with results sent to the clinic.
Sick-day rules: hold metformin and losartan if vomiting, diarrhea or unable to drink, and restart when eating.
Enough medicine, test strips and a printed summary for the journey; message the clinic with readings monthly.

Moderately increased albuminuria (R80.9). Second sample 41 mg/g; one more over three to six months will confirm it. [S]
Repeat in three months with the A1c.

Hypertension (I10). Home 128/80 on losartan; potassium 4.6 and creatinine 1.00, stable. [S]
Continue losartan 25 mg.

Mixed hyperlipidemia (E78.2). He chose a moderate-intensity statin. [S]
Atorvastatin 10 mg daily.
Lipid panel in six to twelve weeks.

Fasting and travel. His fasts with fruit, milk and water have gone safely on metformin. [S]
Continue the same rules; with glucose now steady below 180, a short waterless fast is possible if he drinks well before and after, checks glucose, and breaks it by the same thresholds; avoid waterless fasts in heat or at high altitude.

Insomnia (G47.00). Sleep diary: about two hours to fall asleep, five hours of sleep, rising before dawn for meditation; STOP-BANG 2 (low risk of sleep apnea). Insomnia Severity Index 15. [S]
Cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia by video while he travels: a fixed rising time kept with his meditation, time in bed matched to sleep, and no reading or writing in bed.
No sleeping tablets, as he prefers.

Follow-up: Messages with home readings monthly while he travels. A1c, urine albumin and lipid panel in about three months wherever he is. Diabetes review on his return. Next scheduled visit 2026-10-27: review after seven months away and a week after an asthma attack: A1c, kidneys, lipids, spirometry with bronchodilator response and FeNO; asthma and diabetic kidney disease confirmed; empagliflozin and maintenance-and-reliever inhaler; fasting plan for the coming festival. [S]
